cards.back: Structured vetting of a vendor before engagement: security, compliance, viability, references, and background.
EOI gauges market interest upfront; RFI requests general information on capabilities.
RFP requests a solution proposal; RFQ requests a price for an already-defined service.
Personal interest or another engagement that influences vendor selection: must be disclosed and addressed.
Centralized inventory of third parties, their access, contracts, and internal/external owners.
Service-level agreement: contractual commitment to measurable service levels with remedies for breach.
Service-level objective: numerical target (availability, latency) serving as the benchmark for the SLA.
Non-disclosure agreement: prohibits disclosure of exchanged information and restricts its use.
MOU = intent to cooperate, low commitment; MOA = more binding obligations and responsibilities.
Master services agreement: enduring general terms applicable to all engagements.
Statement of work: describes a specific engagement — scope, deliverables, schedule, pricing. Attaches to the MSA.
Signed rules bounding a test: scope, techniques, hours, contacts, and emergency stop.
Clause authorizing verification of the vendor's controls via documentation or on-site.
Formal declaration accompanied by a report (SOC 2, ISO 27001) proving adherence to a framework.
Continuous measurement of contractual metrics: availability, latency, recovery times.
Periodic review of the security, compliance, and performance of a selected vendor.
Dependency making exit costly or impossible in the short term; addressed via exit clauses and open formats.
Staffing, resource availability, environment, jurisdiction, ROI, insurance, lock-in, and ROE.
